reconcile.connective: Defenders answer that leprosy was conveyed by contact alone, so the king could converse with the excluded Gehazi at a distance, at the gate or in a garden.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells, who catalogued this pairing, presses that a man cursed with permanent leprosy 'as white as snow' in 2 Kings 5:27 should not be found recounting Elisha's deeds to the king in 2 Kings 8:4.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.work: Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "Did God give Gehazi (Elisha's servant) leprosy?" (skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/gehazi.html)
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "Did God give Gehazi (Elisha's servant) leprosy?"

excerpts.excerpt_text: Ceremonial pollution being conveyed by contact alone, there was nothing to prevent a conference being held with this leper at a distance; and although he was excluded from the town of Samaria, this reported conversation may have taken place at the gate or in one of the royal gardens.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly answers the Levitical-purity objection: leprosy spreads only by contact, so a distant conference with the town-excluded Gehazi was possible at the gate or a garden. The single strongest on-tension harmonization on the row.

pd_work.resource: Jamieson, Fausset & Brown, Commentary Critical and Explanatory on the Whole Bible (1871), on 2 Kings 8:4
pd_work.author: Jamieson, Fausset & Brown
pd_work.note: Treats this exact pairing, harmonizing via contact-only contagion and a conference held at a distance from the town-excluded Gehazi. (Haley's specific coverage of this pair unconfirmed; row-surfaced harmonizing commentator anchored per spec.)
